paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: God's heart is wide open, and Paul wants ours to be too. Paul urges that petitions, prayers, intercessions, and thanksgiving be offered "for everyone," even for kings and all those in authority (1 Timothy 2:1-2). Why? Because God our Savior "wants everyone to be saved and to come to the knowledge of the truth" (1 Timothy 2:4). So when I pray for the person who cut me off in traffic, I'm not being nice, I'm lining up with what God already wants.

And there's no side door to God. Paul says "there is one God, and there is one mediator between God and men, the man Christ Jesus," who "gave Himself as a ransom for all" (1 Timothy 2:5-6). One mediator, one ransom, for ALL. That's why Paul was appointed to carry this news to the Gentiles (1 Timothy 2:7), and it's why we pray without anger or dissension (1 Timothy 2:8). If God's invitation goes out to everyone, I can't be hot about the people He's inviting.

Then Paul gets practical, and he says, "I do not permit a woman to teach or to exercise authority over a man; she is to remain quiet," pointing back to Adam being formed first, and then Eve (1 Timothy 2:12-13). This part is weighty, so I'd rather read it slowly than rush it. He ends with a word that women will be saved through childbearing "if they continue in faith, love, and holiness, with self-control" (1 Timothy 2:15). What shines through is a life shaped by God: prayer, peace, good deeds (1 Timothy 2:10) and a faith that keeps going, and that's what I want to bring into the bakery today.
